{"episodes":[{"ep":7,"title":"The Seal in the Storm","script":"SFX: [en] Hurricane wind tears canvas loose. Timber cracks. Rain hammers metal.
SETTLER: [en] Clerk! Your country promised us houses. My daughter is standing in water. Give us the keys!
EWAN: [en] There are no houses.
SETTLER: [en] Then you sold us graves.
INES: [en] Everyone away from the shelter! The roof is lifting!
SFX: [en] A wooden beam crashes. People scream.
EWAN: [en] Take the children toward the trees!
INES: [en] Not the trees. The ground is sliding. Follow my voice and keep low.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] My husband cannot stand.
EWAN: [en] Put his arm over my shoulder.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] You said there would be a hospital.
EWAN: [en] I know what I said.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] Say what is here.
EWAN: [en] Nothing.
SFX: [en] Thunder detonates overhead.
NARRATOR: [en] By midnight, the hurricane had torn the abandoned trading shelter in half. One hundred and seventy-three settlers had arrived. Those still able to walk gathered on a strip of stone above the flood.
SFX: [en] Rainwater sloshes in a cooking pot. A spoon scrapes the empty bottom.
SETTLER: [en] Four handfuls of meal.
INES: [en] For how many?
SETTLER: [en] One hundred and sixty-one answered the count.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] Thirty-eight are children.
EWAN: [en] Divide it among the children.
SETTLER: [en] And tomorrow?
EWAN: [en] There is a trading post north of the inlet.
INES: [en] Twelve miles in this weather.
EWAN: [en] You said they keep grain and salt fish.
INES: [en] They trade for recognised coin. Your families brought Briarhaven paper.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] We brought British sovereigns. Elspeth took them in Edinburgh and gave us these.
SFX: [en] Wet banknotes slap into Ewan’s hand.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] Twenty pounds. Every note stamped by your bank.
EWAN: [en] There is no bank.
SETTLER: [en] Louder, clerk. Let the children hear what purchased their supper.
EWAN: [en] There is no Briarhaven bank. These notes cannot be redeemed.
VOICES: [en] Thief! Shame! He signed them! Take his coat! Search him!
SFX: [en] A fist strikes Ewan. He falls against wet stone.
INES: [en] Enough!
SETTLER: [en] He knew.
EWAN: [en] Yes.
SFX: [en] The crowd quiets under the rain.
EWAN: [en] I knew no Edinburgh bank would redeem them. I said so once, and then I kept preparing other papers because Gregor held my mother’s debt.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] Your mother has a roof.
EWAN: [en] If we remain here, none of us will.
SETTLER: [en] You expect us to follow you?
EWAN: [en] No. I expect you to follow Ines. I will go to the trading post.
INES: [en] You cannot carry enough food alone.
EWAN: [en] Then choose six people who still have strength.
SETTLER: [en] I will not obey a Briarhaven clerk.
INES: [en] Good. Obey the woman who knows which river will drown you. Six people, rope around the waist, now.
SFX: [en] Wind gusts. Rope is pulled from a crate.
NARRATOR: [en] They left before dawn. Behind them, the settlers burned land certificates for warmth. The ink turned green before the paper blackened. Remember that.
SFX: [en] Boots drag through flooded mud. Fast river water roars nearby.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] Stop. My rope is caught.
EWAN: [en] Hold still.
INES: [en] Water is rising. Cut it.
EWAN: [en] Then she loses the line.
INES: [en] Cut it, Ewan.
SFX: [en] Knife saws through rope. A surge of water. Ewan grunts.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] He has me!
INES: [en] Both of you, up the bank!
SFX: [en] Hands scrape over stones. Three bodies collapse in mud.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] Why did you come after our ship?
EWAN: [en] To prove the fraud before you landed.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] You were late.
EWAN: [en] By forty-three days.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] Then do not be late again.
SFX: [en] A trading-post bell clatters in the wind. A heavy door opens on a chain.
TRADING POST KEEPER: [en] Store is closed.
INES: [en] There are starving families at the southern inlet. We need meal, beans, salt fish and lamp oil.
TRADING POST KEEPER: [en] Payment first.
EWAN: [en] We have Briarhaven banknotes.
TRADING POST KEEPER: [en] Then you have kindling.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] These are twenty-pound notes.
TRADING POST KEEPER: [en] Yesterday, three men offered me the same notes. Same number on every one. B-417.
EWAN: [en] Five hundred were printed with that number.
TRADING POST KEEPER: [en] You know your rubbish precisely.
EWAN: [en] I helped make it.
SFX: [en] The door chain tightens.
TRADING POST KEEPER: [en] Then my courtesy to you is this: leave before the coastal patrol arrives.
INES: [en] We are not asking you to accept false money. Extend provisions against the ship’s stores.
TRADING POST KEEPER: [en] The ship is grounded and its cargo is under salvage claim.
EWAN: [en] Against my personal undertaking, then.
TRADING POST KEEPER: [en] Your name?
EWAN: [en] Ewan Pell.
TRADING POST KEEPER: [en] Occupation?
EWAN: [en] Clerk.
TRADING POST KEEPER: [en] Property?
EWAN: [en] None.
TRADING POST KEEPER: [en] Thank you for saving my time.
SFX: [en] Door begins to close.
EWAN: [en] Wait.
SFX: [en] Leather pouch opens. Metal knocks against wood.
INES: [en] Ewan, no.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] What is that?
EWAN: [en] The official seal of Briarhaven.
INES: [en] The seal you proved was made in an Edinburgh workshop.
EWAN: [en] The settlers do not need proof tonight. They need food.
INES: [en] If you stamp a requisition, you use the fraud as authority.
EWAN: [en] I know.
INES: [en] If armed men honour it, they may later demand the territory named on it.
EWAN: [en] I know.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] My daughter has not eaten since yesterday morning.
SFX: [en] Nothing. Long.
EWAN: [en] Keeper, give me one sheet and an ink pad.
TRADING POST KEEPER: [en] I will give you neither.
EWAN: [en] Then I will write on the back of my land grant.
SFX: [en] Paper unfolds. Pencil scratches rapidly.
EWAN: [en] Forty sacks of meal. Twelve sacks of beans. Six barrels of salt fish. Medical spirits and oil. Requisitioned for the relief of Briarhaven settlers under emergency authority.
INES: [en] There is no emergency authority.
EWAN: [en] Tonight there is my name beneath it.
SFX: [en] Seal presses into softened wax.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] You used it.
EWAN: [en] Yes.
EWAN: [en] Keeper, you have my signature, the seal and the names of one hundred and sixty-one survivors. Open the store.
SFX: [en] Paper is examined. Wind whistles through the doorway.
TRADING POST KEEPER: [en] This is carefully prepared.
EWAN: [en] Then honour it.
TRADING POST KEEPER: [en] I cannot.
EWAN: [en] Children will die twelve miles from your door.
TRADING POST KEEPER: [en] I am sorry for them.
EWAN: [en] Send the requisition to your coastal authority. Let them charge Briarhaven.
TRADING POST KEEPER: [en] That is precisely the problem, Mr Pell.
TRADING POST KEEPER: [en] The requisition is rejected because the coastal authorities have never recognized Briarhaven as a country."},{"ep":8,"title":"The Clerk of the Survivors","script":"SFX: [en] Wagon wheels grind over a wooden bridge. A sentry’s bell rings twice.
SENTRY: [en] Halt the convoy! No one enters Crownwater without a receiving order.
EWAN: [en] There are one hundred and fifty-nine survivors behind me. Open the gate.
SENTRY: [en] I said halt.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] Two died while your flag was in sight.
INES: [en] Send for Edwin Codd. Tell him the people sold Briarhaven land have reached his boundary.
SENTRY: [en] Briarhaven officials report through the diplomatic office.
EWAN: [en] There are no Briarhaven officials.
SFX: [en] Survivors murmur. A child coughs violently.
EDWIN: [en] Who said that?
SFX: [en] Measured boots approach along the bridge.
EWAN: [en] I did. Ewan Pell, formerly a clerk in Gregor Vale’s office.
EDWIN: [en] Formerly?
EWAN: [en] If I am still employed, you may hang me after the children have eaten.
EDWIN: [en] This colony does not hang men to improve their grammar. How many sick?
INES: [en] Fifty-three cannot walk. Seventeen have fever. Six children are fading.
EDWIN: [en] Names?
EWAN: [en] Recorded here.
SFX: [en] A damp ledger is handed over.
EDWIN: [en] This says one hundred and seventy-three landed.
EWAN: [en] Fourteen are dead.
EDWIN: [en] And the remaining one hundred and fifty-nine followed you here?
SETTLER: [en] We followed Ines. We tolerated him.
EDWIN: [en] An important administrative distinction.
EWAN: [en] Will you admit them?
EDWIN: [en] Not as citizens of Briarhaven.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] We do not care what you call us.
EDWIN: [en] You will when a merchant charges your food to a government that does not exist. I need a lawful category.
EWAN: [en] Shipwrecked British subjects.
EDWIN: [en] Their ship did not sink.
INES: [en] Their country did.
SFX: [en] Nothing. Brief.
EDWIN: [en] Sentry, enter them as distressed passengers pending individual examination. Open the gate.
SFX: [en] Gate chains run. Heavy doors swing inward.
VOICES: [en] Thank God. Water. Make room. Carry the boy first.
EDWIN: [en] Medical station, thirty-eight children. Kitchens, prepare one hundred and fifty-nine portions. No merchant is to take a note or land certificate as payment.
SETTLER: [en] We have nothing else.
EDWIN: [en] Today, you do not pay.
SFX: [en] The survivors break into exhausted applause and sobbing.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] Say it again, sir. Let the clerk hear.
EDWIN: [en] The survivors are admitted. Food, shelter and treatment will be provided under the Crownwater distress account.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] Fourteen did not reach it.
EDWIN: [en] Their names will be entered too.
NARRATOR: [en] The first meal was served before noon. For the first time since the ship grounded, no Briarhaven paper changed hands.
SFX: [en] Tin bowls and spoons. A ladle strikes a pot.
CHILD: [en] Is this from our farm?
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] No, love.
CHILD: [en] When do we go to our sixty acres?
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] Eat first.
EWAN: [en] I signed the grant for those sixty acres.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] I know.
EWAN: [en] There is no farm.
CHILD: [en] Then why is my name on the paper?
SFX: [en] Spoon drops into a bowl.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] Go and help your brother.
SFX: [en] Small footsteps recede.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] You want forgiveness because you brought us through the marsh.
EWAN: [en] No.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] What do you want?
EWAN: [en] Every certificate, note and appointment they sold you.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] They are all we have left.
EWAN: [en] They are evidence.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] Evidence belongs to courts. Those papers contain our names.
EWAN: [en] Then keep them. Let me record their numbers.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] Why should we trust your record?
EDWIN: [en] Because it will be made in public, under my seal, with each owner standing beside him.
SFX: [en] Chair legs scrape over a stone floor. A crowded hall settles.
EDWIN: [en] This examination is open. The survivors may hear every question and every answer.
EWAN: [en] I ask that Ines remain beside the table.
EDWIN: [en] Granted.
INES: [en] I will correct him when he becomes convenient.
EDWIN: [en] Mr Pell, did a functioning government receive these settlers at the Briarhaven capital?
EWAN: [en] No.
EDWIN: [en] Did you find a harbour?
EWAN: [en] No.
EDWIN: [en] Government house?
EWAN: [en] No.
EDWIN: [en] Barracks, hospital or cathedral?
EWAN: [en] None.
EDWIN: [en] Any resident official empowered to recognise land claims?
EWAN: [en] None.
EDWIN: [en] What did exist?
EWAN: [en] An abandoned trading shelter, promotional maps and a boundary marker dated 1831.
INES: [en] I witnessed the marker and can identify its location.
EDWIN: [en] Recorded. Mr Pell, did you prepare Briarhaven documents?
EWAN: [en] Yes.
EDWIN: [en] Speak so the rear benches hear you.
EWAN: [en] I prepared land grants, commissions and bond certificates. I engraved the seal. I knew the banknotes could not be redeemed. I continued because Gregor Vale held my mother’s unpaid debt ledger and threatened her home.
VOICES: [en] Shame! He admits it! Fourteen dead!
SETTLER: [en] Put him outside the gate!
EDWIN: [en] Silence. Public testimony is not public revenge.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] His mother kept her home while ours were sold.
EWAN: [en] Her debt is sixteen pounds and eight shillings. I will not prepare another certificate to pay it.
EDWIN: [en] Clerk, enter a witness allowance of twenty pounds for Ewan Pell.
EWAN: [en] I do not want payment.
EDWIN: [en] That was not the question. The allowance is lawful compensation for guiding a distressed convoy and giving evidence.
EWAN: [en] Then issue sixteen pounds and eight shillings directly to my mother’s creditor in Edinburgh. Mark the debt discharged. Send the remainder to her.
EDWIN: [en] You understand that once dispatched, it cannot be reclaimed for your passage?
EWAN: [en] Dispatch it today.
SFX: [en] Pen scratches. Sand scatters across wet ink.
EDWIN: [en] Draft authorised. Mara Bell’s debt will be discharged without another Briarhaven certificate.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] That saves your mother.
EWAN: [en] It does not excuse me.
EDWIN: [en] Good. Excuses are difficult to index.
SFX: [en] Bundles of paper are placed on the table.
EDWIN: [en] First claimant.
SETTLER: [en] Forty acres, certificate C-208. I paid thirty sovereigns.
EWAN: [en] The signature is mine. The seal came from the Edinburgh plate.
EDWIN: [en] Second claimant.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] Appointment as schoolmistress. Annual salary, seventy pounds.
EWAN: [en] Same paper stock as the bank charter. No office issued it.
EDWIN: [en] Third.
SETTLER: [en] Ten notes, serial B-417.
EWAN: [en] The number was duplicated five hundred times.
VOICES: [en] Five hundred? They sold me the same number! Mine too!
EDWIN: [en] Mr Pell, can any other witness identify these production marks?
EWAN: [en] Ada Wren can, if she is alive. Her print shop was emptied after she gave me a duplicate plate.
EDWIN: [en] Do you possess that plate?
SFX: [en] Metal plate lands heavily on the table.
EWAN: [en] Yes.
EDWIN: [en] Let the record state that the same damaged border appears on the land grants, banknotes and military commissions.
SETTLER WOMAN: [en] Then say what he is, sir. Not what he pretended to be.
EDWIN: [en] Ewan Pell is the clerk who can identify the forged Briarhaven papers, and this administration accepts his testimony on that basis.
SFX: [en] The hall erupts in argument, then settles under Edwin’s gavel.
EDWIN: [en] Look carefully at what you brought across the ocean.
EDWIN: [en] Ewan’s certificates are the only documents linking your names to land that does not exist."},{"ep":9,"title":"The Green Cross","script":"SFX: [en] Printing presses thunder. Street sellers shout over a London crowd.
STREET SELLER: [en] Second Briarhaven bond issue! New administration confirmed! Traitor clerk exposed!
EWAN: [en] Give me that sheet.
STREET SELLER: [en] One penny.
EWAN: [en] It carries my name.
STREET SELLER: [en] Then you should have bought the first copy.
SFX: [en] Coin clicks. Newspaper snaps open.
INES: [en] Read the official words.
EWAN: [en] “The rumours brought from Crownwater by a dismissed junior clerk have no bearing upon the lawful government of Briarhaven.”
INES: [en] Dismissed.
EWAN: [en] Gregor refused to accept my resignation. Now he has invented one.
INES: [en] Keep reading.
EWAN: [en] “A second issue of bonds will finance the capital’s restoration following storm damage.” Restoration. There was never a capital.
STREET SELLER: [en] The hall opens at twelve. Banker speaking. Soldier speaking. New lady official speaking.
EWAN: [en] What lady official?
STREET SELLER: [en] Buy tomorrow’s sheet.
SFX: [en] Ewan seizes the seller’s bundle. Papers scatter.
STREET SELLER: [en] Thief!
INES: [en] Ewan, here. Bottom of the announcement.
EWAN: [en] “Acting Superintendent of State Printing—Ada Wren.”
SFX: [en] The printing presses continue behind a sudden silence.
INES: [en] Is that the woman who gave you the plate?
EWAN: [en] Yes.
INES: [en] You said she vanished.
EWAN: [en] She did.
INES: [en] Then either they found her or she found them.
EWAN: [en] Ada proved every institution came from one workshop. She would never validate another issue.
INES: [en] You knew her before she disappeared. You do not know what happened after.
EWAN: [en] I am going inside.
STREET SELLER: [en] Not dressed like that.
EWAN: [en] I was invited by the people whose names Gregor printed.
SFX: [en] A folded petition opens.
INES: [en] One hundred and fifty-nine survivor signatures.
NARRATOR: [en] Six weeks after the Crownwater gate opened, the survivors’ testimony reached London. Gregor answered it with engraved invitations, a balcony and another two hundred thousand pounds of paper.
SFX: [en] Carriage doors slam outside a packed subscription hall. Coins and conversation fill the room.
USHER: [en] Invitation.
EWAN: [en] Petition from the surviving Briarhaven settlers.
USHER: [en] Petitions enter through the rear office.
EWAN: [en] The sale is taking place in this room.
USHER: [en] Subscribers enter through this door. Complaints enter tomorrow.
INES: [en] Fourteen people cannot complain tomorrow.
USHER: [en] Madam, I am certain your observation is sincerely intended.
SILAS: [en] Let them pass.
EWAN: [en] Silas.
SILAS: [en] Ewan. You have acquired a tan and a very expensive reputation.
EWAN: [en] Stop the issue.
SILAS: [en] I move paper. I do not stop weather.
EWAN: [en] Gregor is calling the absence of a city storm damage.
SILAS: [en] Buyers prefer repair costs to existential questions.
EWAN: [en] How many bonds have moved?
SILAS: [en] Eight hundred reserved before breakfast. Ninety pounds issue price.
INES: [en] The first issue was eighty.
SILAS: [en] Disaster has increased confidence.
EWAN: [en] You heard the Crownwater testimony.
SILAS: [en] I read a clerk’s allegation and an administrator’s cautious record.
EWAN: [en] One hundred and fifty-nine survivors signed this.
SILAS: [en] And several thousand investors did not.
EWAN: [en] The papers are forged.
SILAS: [en] Then you should not have made them so handsome.
SFX: [en] A ceremonial staff strikes the floor three times.
COMPERE: [en] Gentlemen, subscribers and friends of Briarhaven, please welcome the Cazique, Gregor Vale!
SFX: [en] Applause swells.
GREGOR: [en] My friends, I am told that a storm has made our young country controversial.
VOICES: [en] Shame on the liars! Long live Briarhaven!
GREGOR: [en] Storms are not unusual. Ambition is. Britain did not build her commerce by trusting every frightened clerk who returned from a difficult journey.
EWAN: [en] Fourteen settlers are dead!
SFX: [en] The crowd reacts. A gavel pounds.
GREGOR: [en] Ewan Pell. How welcome.
EWAN: [en] Say their number.
GREGOR: [en] You have interrupted a financial presentation.
EWAN: [en] One hundred and seventy-three sailed. One hundred and fifty-nine reached Crownwater. Say how many died in the country you sold them.
GREGOR: [en] The tropics are demanding.
EWAN: [en] There is no capital, harbour, hospital or government.
GREGOR: [en] You abandoned your assigned post before the administration could complete its preparations.
EWAN: [en] I stood on the mapped site. There was one ruined shelter.
INES: [en] I guided him there. I know that coast.
GREGOR: [en] And you are?
INES: [en] The person your guidebooks forgot to invent.
VOICES: [en] Let her speak! Remove them! What happened to the loan?
CYRUS: [en] Subscribers, the bank’s validation remains in force. The first loan was assessed upon the instruments submitted, not upon theatrical reports from unidentified traders.
EWAN: [en] Then identify one physical asset securing it.
CYRUS: [en] The territorial grant.
EWAN: [en] The boundary marker predates Gregor’s claimed grant by three years.
GREGOR: [en] According to whom?
EWAN: [en] According to the date cut into the stone.
GREGOR: [en] Stones are often reused.
EWAN: [en] So are your banknote numbers.
SFX: [en] Laughter and angry shouting divide the hall.
SILAS: [en] Gentlemen, subscriptions are still being accepted at the side tables.
EWAN: [en] Close those tables.
SILAS: [en] That authority does not belong to you.
EWAN: [en] It does not belong to any person in this room.
GREGOR: [en] There you are mistaken. Briarhaven’s civil administration has continued throughout this unfortunate disturbance.
EWAN: [en] Name one official who has governed from Briarhaven.
GREGOR: [en] Administration is not confined by geography.
EWAN: [en] Then show us the official.
GREGOR: [en] With pleasure.
SFX: [en] Gregor rings a small silver bell.
GREGOR: [en] You accused me of hiding the machinery of government. Today, you may inspect it.
EWAN: [en] Ada is not your machinery.
GREGOR: [en] Curious. I had not yet said her name.
SFX: [en] The crowd murmurs. Camera powder flares with a muffled pop.
EWAN: [en] Where is she?
GREGOR: [en] Mr Pell, your concern arrives after a long voyage. She remained in Britain and accepted responsibility.
EWAN: [en] Her father’s shop was stripped bare.
GREGOR: [en] Businesses fail. Talented daughters improve their circumstances.
EWAN: [en] Let me speak to her alone.
GREGOR: [en] An official of her rank cannot be privately examined by a fugitive clerk.
INES: [en] If she is free, ask her to come down.
GREGOR: [en] Threats are unnecessary. Ada has requested to address the subscribers herself.
EWAN: [en] Requested?
GREGOR: [en] You may find her choice disappointing.
SFX: [en] Balcony curtains draw apart above the hall.
VOICES: [en] There she is! The Green Cross! Make way!
EWAN: [en] Ada!
SFX: [en] Nothing. Long.
COMPERE: [en] Ada Wren, Acting Superintendent of State Printing, wearing the Green Cross of Briarhaven.
ADA: [en] Ewan Pell is the traitor who abandoned Briarhaven."}],"beat_sheet":[{"beat_id":"b025","ep":7,"seq":1,"world_time":"1834-05-30","location":"supposed Briarhaven capital site, Sable
